status: Six database articles approved after substantive development; forty-four manuscripts remain held.
publication: Six approved articles released on October 30, 2026. Other draft creation dates do not authorize publication.
voice: Short sentences, familiar words, a conversational voice, and concrete problems. Explain necessary terms. No invented personal incidents, deliberate grammar mistakes, or claims of human-only authorship.
review: Author editorial pass; no independent human authorship or independent reviewer is claimed.
verification_limits: Many Rust blocks are explicitly scoped handler excerpts or data models, not complete applications.
The snippet CI verifies selected self-contained Rust examples directly from MDX; it does not validate every application helper.
New SQL Server permission and import scenarios require live engine checks before runtime verification can be claimed.
Performance pieces describe proposed comparisons and contain no invented timing results.

The existing publication audit requires 700 words for reviewed clustered articles. Forty-four shorter drafts remain reviewed:false. Six database articles now have substantive explanations and complete Rust fixture evidence; see the current release record.

articles.title: Database pool full? Check who is holding the connections.
articles.new_value: Diagnose a request handler that holds a pool connection while it waits for unrelated HTTP work. Separate pool acquisition time from query time before changing the pool size.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust handler fixture with a controlled slow dependency, connection lifetime tracing, and acquisition measurements before and after shortening the checkout scope.

articles.title: Keep HTTP Calls Outside the Checkout Transaction
articles.new_value: Apply transaction boundaries to a checkout that calls a shipping provider. Compare holding stock locks during HTTP with storing durable delivery intent. Explain pending states and recovery.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A controlled provider timeout and a concurrent stock update in Rust. Show committed state and recoverable intent at each crash point; do not claim the outbox makes external effects exactly once.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: Two Webhook Deliveries Need One Database Claim
articles.new_value: Focus on the concurrent check-then-insert race at a webhook endpoint. Add a unique claim and a defined response for repeated identities and changed payloads.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Two Rust requests released by a barrier against the same identity. Assert the committed business effect, the duplicate response, and the changed-payload rejection.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: Use a Separate Database Identity for Migrations
articles.new_value: Turn the owner-versus-application-role distinction into a deployment recipe. Separate schema changes from normal requests and test the application account's denied DDL operations.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust connection checks using separate migration and application credentials. Verify allowed reads and writes as well as rejected schema and policy changes.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: Make an index earn its place in a write-heavy table.
articles.new_value: Make an index retention decision for a frequently updated status column. Compare the important read path with update work rather than treating the HOT counter as a speed score.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust workload with and without the candidate index, read plans, update statistics, recorded settings, and repeated measurements. Keep conclusions within that workload.

articles.title: Put two tenants in your authorization tests.
articles.new_value: Exercise the full API path with colliding record IDs and two users. Cover request context, database role, and denial responses rather than repeating policy syntax.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust API fixtures for allowed and cross-tenant reads and writes, including a pooled connection reused by the other tenant. Assert unchanged data after denial.

articles.title: Return HTTP Success After the Database Commit
articles.new_value: Follow a checkout result through the HTTP response boundary. Distinguish commit failure from a response lost after a successful commit, with a lookup path for the latter.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust endpoint scenarios for rollback, successful commit, and a dropped response after commit. Record persisted state separately from what the client observed.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: A SQLite Import Can Block Normal Saves
articles.new_value: Design an interactive import with bounded transactions, resumable progress, and a busy policy. The decision is how the importer shares write access with foreground saves.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust importer and a foreground writer with controlled contention. Compare transaction lengths and successful foreground progress without asserting that WAL permits concurrent writers.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: Run reports with a database account that cannot write.
articles.new_value: Provide a reporting identity and explicit grants for an existing database. Demonstrate that a reporting bug cannot write to the business tables covered by the policy.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust reporting query plus denied INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and DDL checks using the actual reporting account. Require a real SQL Server service for runtime claims; compilation alone is insufficient.

articles.title: A Rejected PostgreSQL Import Row Needs a Recovery Path
articles.new_value: Add durable per-row outcomes and an explicit quarantine path around a bulk importer. Preserve enough safe context to repair rejected rows without silently discarding them.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust mixed-validity import, a bounded rejection record, and a corrected replay. Specify whether a batch rolls back together or accepts independent rows, and test that contract on a real service.
articles.evidence_produced: Complete Rust fixture and observed CI output in the October 30 release record. The original proposal above is superseded by the final article scope and its explicit limits.

articles.title: Release the mutex before calling a remote API.
articles.new_value: Solve a shared-cache refresh that holds a lock during network work. Copy the request state under a short lock and check whether the state changed before applying the result.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust tasks synchronized with barriers to show blocked access and a stale refresh result. Explain cases that require a different ownership or serialization design.

articles.title: Decide what happens when the queue is full.
articles.new_value: Choose an admission policy for an HTTP endpoint backed by a bounded worker queue. Compare waiting with a deadline, explicit rejection, and durable acceptance.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust endpoint under a deliberately stalled worker. Assert each accepted or rejected request's outcome and show where the waiting work resides.

articles.title: Don't detach a task just to hide a slow request.
articles.new_value: Make request disconnects and task ownership explicit for a slow export. Choose between request-owned cancellation and a durable job rather than dropping the JoinHandle without a policy.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust scenarios for client disconnect, task failure, and service restart. Show which result survives and who observes failures in each design.

articles.title: Set a byte limit before collecting a response body.
articles.new_value: Implement bounded reading for an upstream body whose length is unknown or unreliable. Distinguish a buffering capacity from a maximum accepted payload.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust inputs just below, at, and above the limit, plus a stream with no declared length. Detect overflow without allocating or reading the entire body.

articles.title: One request should not start a thousand tasks at once.
articles.new_value: Bound fan-out in an aggregation endpoint. Limit active work before spawning it and preserve a clear cancellation and result policy.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust instrumentation for maximum active operations and live tasks with a blocked upstream. Compare spawn-all-then-wait with bounded production of work.

articles.title: An Arc clone can keep old data alive longer than you expect.
articles.new_value: Follow a large configuration snapshot retained by queued and slow tasks after replacement. Separate the small inline handle from the heap allocation it keeps alive.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust snapshot with a drop counter and controlled task completion. Show retention and release; do not confuse size_of_val on the handle with total retained memory.

articles.title: Don't use a metrics counter to decide who can book the last place.
articles.new_value: Contrast an observational count with an atomic reservation protocol. Show why reading a count and later incrementing it can over-admit concurrent requests.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust check-then-act race and a corrected reservation primitive. Explain the protocol before choosing ordering, and cover cancellation or failure after a reservation.

articles.title: Send worker failures back to the caller.
articles.new_value: Design the reply path for a worker command. Separate a business error, a closed reply channel, and a crashed worker instead of turning all three into an empty response.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust command/reply examples using Result and a oneshot channel, with successful work, handler failure, dropped sender, and worker panic scenarios.

articles.title: A queue of 100 messages can still use too much memory.
articles.new_value: Size a queue using payload bytes and work already removed by workers. This answers the memory budget question separately from the admission-policy question in article 12.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust workload with uneven payload sizes and a slow consumer. Account for queued, in-flight, and producer-held bytes; include an oversized-message policy.

articles.title: Check whether Drop is making your Rust request slow.
articles.new_value: Diagnose synchronous destructor work on an async request path. Trace scope exit and make expensive cleanup an explicit lifecycle decision.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A deliberately slow Rust destructor and request timing around scope exit. Compare explicit cleanup ownership and shutdown handling without promising that arbitrary cleanup can safely be detached.

articles.title: Keep the broken input before you fix the bug.
articles.new_value: Turn an observed failure into the smallest useful regression fixture before asking an agent to change code. Show the requirement the fixture protects.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A recorded Rust debugging session with the failing input, a failing assertion, and a correction. Preserve evidence that the assertion detects the original bug.

articles.title: A test should fail for the reason you meant.
articles.new_value: Show a test that accepts any database error and goes green because the connection is broken. Assert the intended constraint failure and unchanged persisted state.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust tests covering a real constraint error, an unrelated connection error, and a successful invalid write. The test must distinguish all three.

articles.title: Don't fix a flaky test with a longer sleep.
articles.new_value: Replace timing guesses in a retrying API client test with explicit readiness and controlled time. Keep a separate check for real timeout behaviour.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust tests using a barrier, a local mock transport, and controlled time where supported. Explain why controlling one clock does not control an external service.

articles.title: Don't put a timestamp in the dependency cache key.
articles.new_value: Separate reusable dependency inputs from a run identifier in a Rust CI cache. Account for toolchain, target, profile, and configuration instead of making every restore a guaranteed miss.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Existing GitHub workflow runs showing cache keys, hit or miss, and Cargo dirty reasons. Distinguish dependency reuse from final artifacts whose correctness depends on publication time or other changing inputs.

articles.title: Check the lockfile change before blaming the new Rust compiler.
articles.new_value: Investigate a toolchain upgrade that also changed dependency resolution. Hold the dependency graph fixed where compatible and identify which change introduced the failure.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A small Rust dependency fixture and a CI comparison matrix with recorded lockfiles and toolchains. State when the old dependency graph cannot run on a tested compiler.

articles.title: Test generated code from an empty output directory.
articles.new_value: Catch generated files that survive locally but are absent on a fresh checkout. Make the build script's declared inputs and produced files sufficient on their own.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust CI runs from fresh and reused build directories, with one generator input changed and one output deliberately absent. Do not prescribe routine cache deletion as the fix.

articles.title: Keep the debug symbols for the binary you actually shipped.
articles.new_value: Make a production crash trace resolvable after a release. Connect a deployed executable to the exact symbol artifact, source revision, and retention policy.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust CI artifact pair and a deliberate crash whose addresses are resolved with the matching symbols. Include a mismatched-build check and redact sensitive crash data.

articles.title: Measure tail latency before raising request concurrency.
articles.new_value: Choose a client concurrency limit using queue delay and slow-request behaviour as well as throughput. Follow one fixed workload through several limits.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust client and controlled upstream in GitHub CI, recording throughput, errors, queue wait, and latency distributions. Publish workload and measurement limits with any figures.

articles.title: Change one performance variable at a time.
articles.new_value: Review a search optimization that changed the input set and implementation together. Establish comparable inputs before investigating interactions between changes.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust benchmark matrix in existing GitHub CI, with fixed inputs and separate implementation, pattern, and reporting changes. Include unchanged controls and avoid invented speedups.

articles.title: Should generated API clients live in their own Rust crate?
articles.new_value: Evaluate a specific crate boundary around a generated client and frequently edited service code. Compare clean build cost and representative incremental edits.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Two Rust workspace layouts built in existing GitHub CI with the same generated source, dependencies, and edit sequence. Include a case where the split adds overhead or little benefit.

articles.title: Keep provider status strings out of UI components.
articles.new_value: Follow one account status from a provider response to a product-facing response. Centralize translation and make unknown states visible without spreading provider branches through the interface.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust adapter with known, missing, and new provider states and product-contract assertions. Preserve provider detail where a real product feature needs it.

articles.title: Don't turn every provider 429 into a customer 500.
articles.new_value: Define a product-level error contract for an upstream rate limit. Distinguish whose quota is exhausted, whether work was accepted, and what the caller can usefully do next.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust adapter scenarios for shared upstream quota, customer-specific quota, and temporary unavailability. Do not blindly copy the provider's status or Retry-After header into every response.

articles.title: Choose one layer to own retries.
articles.new_value: Expose retry amplification when a transport, provider SDK, and worker each retry the same operation. Give the operation one effective attempt budget and deadline.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust mock transport counting actual network attempts under nested policies and under a shared policy. Include cancellation and a Retry-After value beyond the remaining deadline.

articles.title: After a timeout, check the outcome before repeating the write.
articles.new_value: Build a client recovery flow for an order that may have committed before the response was lost. Use the provider's documented idempotency and lookup contract instead of treating timeout as proof of failure.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust client against a controlled provider that commits and then drops the response. Show lookup, same-key retry when supported, and the unresolved state when no reliable lookup exists.

articles.title: Don't repair an entire integration inside a GET request.
articles.new_value: Handle a read that discovers drift without turning it into an unbounded repair job. Return an honest state and enqueue bounded repair work when product requirements permit.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust request fixture that discovers missing remote records, deduplicates a repair request, and reports repair progress or failure. Explain when synchronous reconciliation is part of the API contract.

articles.title: Make API cursors opaque and bind them to the query.
articles.new_value: Design a versioned cursor envelope that rejects reuse with another filter or tenant. Preserve stable ordering without exposing the database schema as the public API.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust cursor encode/decode checks for changed filters, tenants, versions, and malformed input. Explain that encoding is not secrecy and a signature does not replace authorization.

articles.title: Put the tenant in the cache key, not just the record ID.
articles.new_value: Follow namespaced identities into an application cache where a database row policy cannot protect an incorrectly shared entry. Include provider or account scope where IDs require it.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust cache with two tenants using the same external ID. Reproduce the collision and assert isolated reads, writes, and invalidation after correcting the key.

articles.title: A bulk response must say which items succeeded.
articles.new_value: Design the public response and retry contract for a partially successful bulk endpoint. Preserve stable per-item identities across response order changes and lost responses.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust endpoint and client with mixed outcomes, reordered results, a missing result, and a repeated item. State whether the endpoint promises atomic or independent item processing.

articles.title: A webhook response should follow durable acceptance.
articles.new_value: Separate HTTP acceptance from later business processing. Persist a received event with a pending state and show how a worker recovers it after a crash.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust crash-point scenarios around durable receipt, HTTP acknowledgement, worker claim, and business commit. A received row must not be mistaken for an applied inbox claim; preserve atomic claim-and-mutate for business effects.

articles.title: Give repair scripts a preview before they write.
articles.new_value: Make an operator-facing repair command show proposed changes, scope, and conflicts before applying them. Check record versions again so the preview cannot authorize stale writes.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust repair CLI with plan and apply phases, a changed record between the phases, and bounded selection. Show rejected stale plans and explicit partial-failure outcomes.

articles.title: Start an internal AI tool with read-only access.
articles.new_value: Describe a staged rollout for one internal assistant that searches records before it can modify them. Define the allowed dataset, identity checks, and evidence required to add a write tool.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust tool gateway with narrow search capability and denied cross-user reads. Explain that read-only access can still expose private data or create resource costs.

articles.title: The model should not choose whose credentials it uses.
articles.new_value: Implement credential selection in server-owned request context. Reject a model-supplied account identifier that attempts to switch the acting user or provider account.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust gateway with authorized and forged account selections and a background-job identity. Assert both the denied effect and the credential actually used for allowed calls.

articles.title: Log the tool decision without copying the customer's document.
articles.new_value: Implement a bounded tool-audit event containing actor scope, decision, policy version, result category, and safe correlation IDs. Keep content capture a separate, explicit decision.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust structured-event fixture with secret canaries in arguments, document text, and error chains. Assert the useful metadata remains while private content is absent from the collected events.

articles.title: Only offer tools that belong to the current workflow.
articles.new_value: Build separate tool manifests for a support lookup and an administrative write workflow. Explain how a smaller offered set reduces accidental actions while server authorization remains mandatory.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust manifest builder and gateway checks for workflow changes and fabricated calls to hidden tools. Do not treat a hidden tool name as an access-control boundary.

articles.title: A denied tool call must leave no side effect.
articles.new_value: Catch validation that runs after a file, database row, or external request was already changed. Assert the effect boundary as well as the error response.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust fixtures for invalid syntax, invalid business arguments, and denied authorization. Check persisted state and mock external-call counts after every rejection.

articles.title: A fallback model must not get wider permissions.
articles.new_value: Follow identity and capabilities through an automatic model fallback after an upstream failure. Prevent a router or default client from substituting a more privileged tool context.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust workflow with a deliberately failing primary transport, a fallback, and a forbidden write attempt. Assert identical authorization constraints and no external effect on both paths.

articles.title: Your agent test should not be able to send a real email.
articles.new_value: Design an end-to-end agent environment whose mail effects are captured by a test adapter. Bind credentials and destinations to the environment, and fail closed if production configuration appears.
articles.evidence_to_produce: Rust adapter selection checks and a forbidden production-destination case with no live mail credential. Explain that a fake adapter does not verify real provider delivery.

articles.title: Even a trusted tool needs an output limit.
articles.new_value: Bound tool results before they enter model context or traces. Provide pagination or an explicit truncation response so a partial result cannot quietly look complete.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A Rust tool gateway with oversized rows, long strings, and many pages. Verify byte and item limits, truncation metadata, and continuation behaviour before constructing the model request.

articles.title: Don't delete the eval case that made the release look bad.
articles.new_value: Create a review policy for keeping fixed failures and changing obsolete evaluation cases. Preserve a reason, expected behaviour, and version history rather than removing difficult examples to improve the score.
articles.evidence_to_produce: A small replay dataset with a reproduced regression, a corrected version, and a genuinely obsolete requirement. Show the review record for retaining, updating, or retiring each case.

articles.title: An overall eval score can hide the workflow you broke.
articles.new_value: Make a release decision for two workflows when a common easy path improves but a smaller important path regresses. Report paired comparisons by workflow and the actual number of cases.
articles.evidence_to_produce: An explicitly synthetic, versioned dataset with aggregate improvement and a workflow regression. Show sample sizes and uncertainty; do not imply a tiny slice provides a precise statistical estimate.
